title: Activation-conditioned rescale pipeline + runtime kernel shim for INT8 calibration
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need an activation-conditioned rescale pipeline that produces per-layer/channel rescale profiles for INT8 conversion (activation-aware approach) and a minimal runtime kernel shim to support the rescale during inference without regressing KV-cache-heavy workloads. This ticket covers the calibration harness, offline profile storage format, validation harness (quality + perf), and a backwards-compatible runtime shim that applies the rescale and falls back to FP16 when necessary.

Context and motivation:
Previous INT8 calibration efforts showed promising latency/cost improvements but suffered accuracy regressions on a subset of decoder-only LLMs due to activation distribution mismatch at inference (especially with long KV cache and variable sequence lengths). Existing PRs (see ENG-5421, ENG-91456) implement layer-wise calibration, but we need a coordinated pipeline that: 1) produces stable per-channel rescale factors informed by activation statistics collected under representative KV/cache patterns, 2) ships a compact profile format, and 3) provides a runtime shim that minimizes code churn and keeps latency within SLOs.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- A calibration pipeline that outputs per-layer/channel float rescale profiles (JSON+binary blob) with metadata (model-version, seq-len-window, dataset-tag).
- An offline evaluator that validates quality impact on our eval suite (redwood/evals/coherence & redwood/evals/mt) with: mean log-likelihood delta <= 0.5% and task-specific metric drops <= 0.7% relative to FP16 baseline.
- Runtime kernel shim that applies activation rescale before quantized matmul and restores scaling as needed with <1.5% average token latency increase on production 8xA100 pools and <5% throughput degradation under typical batching.
- CI gated: end-to-end calibration -> runtime integration tests and perf benchmark (latency, p95) added to the quantization pipeline.
- Rollout plan: staged rollout (canary 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic revert if accuracy/regressions exceed thresholds.

Design overview:
1) Calibration harness:
   - Collector runs on sample generation traces: generate representative KV cache distributions (short, medium, long prompt tails).
   - Collect per-activation statistics (abs-mean, RMS, max) per channel for attention:q,k,v and MLP activations.
   - Compute rescale factors following the activation-conditioned formula (channel_scale = sqrt(E[act^2] / (E[weight^2] + eps))).
   - Store profiles as compact format: metadata JSON + compressed float16 array per layer.

2) Profile selection and metadata:
   - Profiles tagged by model-version, seq-len-bucket, quant-mode (symmetric/asymmetric), data-tag.
   - Lookup logic in runtime picks the nearest seq-len-bucket and model-version fallback table.

3) Runtime shim (minimal invasive approach):
   - Implement as a lightweight pre/post op surrounding the quantized GEMM kernel: multiply incoming activation by per-channel scale (fused with existing dequantization path where possible).
   - For KV-cache heavy inference, apply scaling only on newly computed tokens (not cached past keys) to avoid redundant ops.
   - Provide a hotspot path that fuses scaling into the dequantize+gemm kernels on CUDA using a small kernel patch/shim with feature flagging.
   - Fallback to FP16 execution (or previous int8 path) if profile missing or if runtime detects accuracy drifting in canary checks.

4) Validation and perf harness:
   - Unit tests for numerical equivalence on a subset of layers.
   - E2E validation: run generation on 10k prompts from eval set and compute log-prob delta + task metrics.
   - Perf bench: p50/p95 token latency under real workload traces and throughput under batch sizes [1,4,8].

5) CI and rollout:
   - New GH actions workflow: quant-calibrate -> upload artifact -> integrate in runtime CI job.
   - Canary rollout gated by automatic quality check (if any eval metric drops beyond thresholds, rollback).

Open decisions / trade-offs considered:
- Whether to store scales as float16 (smaller) vs float32 (numerical stability). We chose float16 with optional fp32 override per-profile metadata.
- Whether to apply scaling globally to both attention and MLP or only attention heads. Initial experiments show attention scaling yields most benefit; we include MLP optional flag.
- Kernel integration strategy: shim vs full fused kernel. Shim chosen for faster iteration and safer rollback.

Acceptance tests / Demo steps:
1) Run calibration on sample model: ./calib/run_calibration --model resnet-llama-7b --traces traces/long-kv.tar.gz
2) Upload profile to internal store and trigger runtime E2E: ./deploy/profile_apply --profile profile-resnet-llama-7b-v1
3) Run redwood-eval suite and ensure metrics within thresholds.
4) Perform canary rollout via console with 5% traffic and watch accuracy dashboard.

Artifacts and references:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Activation+Conditioned+Rescale+Design
- Calibration tool PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/calibration/pull/47
- Runtime shim PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289
- Eval dashboards: https://dash.redwood.ai/evals/quant-rescale-2026-02

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: hidden accuracy regressions for low-resource languages. Mitigation: extend eval corpus and run language-specific checks in canary phase.
- Risk: perf regression on small GPU types. Mitigation: disable rescale shim on constrained pools via runtime feature flags.

Next steps (this ticket):
- Finish runtime shim PR (Liam) and land basic fuse patch for dequant+scale (target: 2026-03-12).
- Expand calibration traces (Sofia) with additional KV patterns by 2026-03-01.
- Add CI gating job for profile artifacts (Noah) by 2026-03-08.
